# SAM

Six filters, applied one at a time, each with a named source. Three are MEASURED or directly observed; three are DERIVED or BOUNDED and are labelled as such. No filter is presented as harder evidence than it is.

## Base: 58,643 registered HEIs

*Source: AISHE 2021-22. Super-bound. Not a market.*

## Filter 1 - Institution type  [DERIVED]

**Question.** Must be a degree-granting body with an innovation function

**Source.** AISHE 2021-22 category counts

**Rule.** universities + colleges; standalone diploma institutes excluded (no innovation mandate)

**Result.** 46,641 to 46,641 institutions survive (drops 12,002-12,002; 79.53%-79.53% of the registered base).

Stand-alone institutions (12,002) are polytechnics, teacher-training and nursing institutes at diploma level. They have no IIC and no NIRF Innovation obligation. Excluding them removes 20% of the registered base.

## Filter 2 - Digital readiness  [DERIVED]

**Question.** Must have institutional internet, not just computers in a room

**Source.** AISHE 2021-22 Box 7 (NKN / NMEICT connectivity)

**Rule.** universities x NKN share + colleges x NKN share

**Result.** 11,567 to 41,102 institutions survive (drops 35,074-5,539; 19.72%-70.09% of the registered base).

THE FINDING. Colleges have a computer centre in 88% of cases but institutional backbone connectivity in only 24%. A cloud product needs the backbone; the upper bound assumes computer-centre presence suffices.

## Filter 3 - Innovation activity  [MEASURED]

**Question.** Must demonstrably file an innovation return

**Source.** NIRF India Rankings 2025, Innovation category

**Rule.** count of institutions that filed the Innovation category in 2025

**Result.** 777 to 777 institutions survive (drops 10,790-40,325; 1.32%-1.32% of the registered base).

The only filter with a directly observed count. Everything upstream of this is a proxy; this is 777 institutions that demonstrably did the work.

## Filter 4 - Budget  [DERIVED]

**Question.** Must be able to afford the contract

**Source.** Union Budget 2025-26; data_p5_finance PRIVATE_COLLEGE_BOUND

**Rule.** Rs 1.2L is 0.0063% of a NIT budget and 0.3% of the LOW end of the bounded private college revenue band

**Result.** 777 to 777 institutions survive (drops 0-0; 1.32%-1.32% of the registered base).

PASSES 100%. This filter excludes nobody, at either price. That is the Phase 5 result restated: affordability has never been the obstacle.

## Filter 5 - Ecosystem maturity  [BOUNDED]

**Question.** Must sit in a state whose startup ecosystem is functional

**Source.** SRF 5.0 tiers

**Rule.** exclude Emerging-tier states (7 of 34); institution counts by state are not public

**Result.** 582 to 777 institutions survive (drops 195-0; 0.99%-1.32% of the registered base).

BOUNDED, not measured. Seven states are Emerging-tier; their share of the 777 is not published. The 25% haircut is an analyst floor, not a measurement. Note the perverse case: Emerging states may be the BEST prospects because they have the most to gain and the least incumbent.

## Filter 6 - Geography  [DERIVED]

**Question.** Must be reachable in the initial selling motion

**Source.** NIRF 2025 regional split; Startup India Tier 2/3 data

**Rule.** exclude the East (7.5% of filers, lowest concentration and most dispersed)

**Result.** 582 to 777 institutions survive (drops 0-0; 0.99%-1.32% of the registered base).

The East holds 7.5% of Innovation filers. Excluding it costs 7.5% of the market and is a distribution decision, not an economic one - the East is where relative improvement is easiest.

## What the funnel actually shows

The funnel terminates at **582-777 institutions** - between 0.99% and 1.32% of all registered higher education.

Three results are worth stating plainly:

1. **Digital readiness, not budget, is where colleges fail.** Colleges have a computer centre in 88% of cases but institutional backbone connectivity in 24%. The upper bound here is generous - it assumes a computer centre is sufficient - and even so it is the largest single reduction in the funnel.
2. **Innovation activity is the binding filter and it is MEASURED.** 777 institutions filed a NIRF Innovation return in 2025. That is observed behaviour, not a proxy, and it is the number the whole sizing rests on.
3. **Budget excludes nobody.** Filter 4 passes 100% of institutions at both prices. This is not a modelling choice - it is the Phase 5 finding restated as a filter. The obstacle has never been affordability.

## Two filters that did not reduce the upper bound

Filters 5 and 6 appear to show 100% survival on the high bound. That is arithmetic, not an oversight: by filter 5 the *low* bound has already been cut to 582 by the ecosystem haircut, so the geography filter cannot reduce it further. Both filters are real and both bite on the low bound.

## Value

| Scenario | Institutions | ACV | SAM value |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | 582-777 | Rs 120,000 | Rs 7.0-9.3 cr |
| B | 582-777 | Rs 1,027,962 | Rs 59.8-79.9 cr |

The measured 777-institution count is retained as a cross-check: at Scenario A it is Rs 9.3 crore, at Scenario B Rs 79.9 crore.
